trust_decision.summary: A server-side fetch of the operator-set media service base URL (media::url) is exempted from the safeurl wrapper's private-IP classification only for that URL's host, and every other destination must be classified; the decision input is the safeUrlAllow entry handed to @tak-ps/node-safeurl's fetch at 9 call sites in api/lib/control/video-service.ts, with the matching rule itself supplied by the dependency bumped 1.4.0 -> 1.5.0.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names an SSRF in the basemap import (PUT /api/basemap), so the first place an engineer looks is importBasemapURL, whose only IP-classification is an isSafeUrl call that is already present at the pinned commit and is not changed by this fix; the graded fix actually lands in api/lib/control/video-service.ts, so the summary and the diff point at different modules.

fix_sites.entry_point: none - recordings() has no caller in api/routes at the pinned commit

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The CoTAK provider URL is an admin-only setting for a neighbouring optional SSO feature, not the media service the advisory names, and the published commit left it untouched - so a solver can argue that route was never covered.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Every media fetch target is rebuilt from media::url with the port forced to 9997, so the exemption must be keyed on host only; a fix that compares full origin (scheme+port) or that runs isSafeUrl over media::url breaks the supported Docker-Compose deployment where the media server is reached on a private/internal hostname ('media' is special-cased at line 238).

O6_input_shapes: URL with a path or trailing slash (e.g. 'https://video.example.com/') - new URL(...).hostname strips the path
URL with an explicit port (e.g. 'http://media:9997') - hostname strips the port, which the 9997-forced fetch targets require
scheme+host only in a plain string (e.g. 'http://media-server', the shape used by api/test/video-lease.srv.test.ts:86-88)
mixed-case or IP-literal host - URL parsing normalises the hostname before it is handed to the allow list

O8_uncovered_routes.route: CoTAK user-provider calls (token, machine user, agency, channel) still pass the full provider URL as safeUrlAllow - 14 sites in the same api package after the 1.5.0 bump
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: CoTAK is an optional SSO/user provider ('provider::url' is another admin setting); the advisory and the commit are about the media service, so this looks like a neighbouring feature.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package (api), different module directory (lib/user vs lib/control); producer at api/lib/user/cotak.ts:41-58

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Events task fetches the ETL API URL with a full-URL safeUrlAllow entry (and repeats it through transform/worker/index)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: tasks/events is a separate package that still pins @tak-ps/node-safeurl ^1.4.0 (tasks/events/package.json:21) and was not part of the 1.5.0 upgrade, so the hostname contract arguably does not apply to it.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different top-level package (tasks/events), own package.json and lockfile

O8_uncovered_routes.route: PMTiles task fetches CloudTAK API URLs with safeUrlAllow set to the whole API_URL
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: tasks/pmtiles is a separate package still on ^1.4.0 and the allow target is its own deployment-configured API_URL, not user input.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different top-level package (tasks/pmtiles), own package.json and lockfile

O8b_injection_room.sibling: fetches a basemap tile URL taken from an imported basemap via node-safeurl fetch; a sibling would add safeUrlAllow: [tile host] for an internal tile server
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Internal/on-prem tile servers are a normal CloudTAK deployment, and the same author already writes URL-keyed allow entries in the media and provider code.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second user-provider implementation under api/lib/user that also allow-lists its configured base URL
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: cotak.ts is already that shape (interface-user.ts:111 picks a provider), so adding another provider or a wrapper around CoTAK needs the same hostname normalisation.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the TileJSON fetch of a user-supplied basemap URL; a sibling would exempt an operator's internal basemap host via safeUrlAllow
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The route already gates this fetch with isSafeUrl (api/routes/basemap.ts:92-95), so a maintainer adding 'our intranet basemaps are fine' would use the same allow-list mechanism.

O9_family: SSRF (CWE-918): server-side request to an allow-listed destination bypasses IP classification

O10_build.toolchain: npm + tsc for api (api/package.json:11 build), tests via tsx --test with StackName=test (api/package.json:8); Node >= 24 (api/package.json:23-25)
services: TAK server for the video tests (api/test/video-lease.srv.test.ts:8 flight.init({takserver:true}))
media server mocked in-process with undici MockAgent (api/test/video-lease.srv.test.ts:35-92)
O10_build.project_tests: api/test/video-lease.srv.test.ts, api/test/connection-video-lease.srv.test.ts, api/test/profile-video.srv.test.ts - pre-existing and already cover the media-service routes with a mocked media host; the fix adds no tests.

j.j_sites_touched: api/lib/control/video-service.ts (plus api/package.json and package-lock.json dependency bump)
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Validate media::url with isSafeUrl (or reject private/IP hosts) in PUT /api/config or in settings() before the fetch, which blocks the intended internal Docker-Compose media host.

out_of_scope_notes: The advisory summary describes an SSRF in PUT /api/basemap; that route's isSafeUrl guard (api/routes/basemap.ts:92-95) is untouched by this fix and was not screened as part of it.
unverified: node-safeurl 1.5.0's matching rule (hostname equality vs origin/prefix) lives inside the dependency and node_modules is absent with no network allowed, so whether the remaining full-URL safeUrlAllow entries are a live bypass or merely a functional break in api/lib/user/cotak.ts could not be determined.
Repository size in MB could not be measured (no shell in this session), so the tiny_repo/giant_repo red flags were left unset.

The fix's own regression behaviour is not testable from the tree: api/lib/control/video-service.ts:805 recordings() has no caller in api/routes at the pinned commit, so the changed site at :817 is unreachable from any route.
